prompt:
TEASER 16 | PREPARING THE MACHINE
DURATION 20 SECONDS | HORIZONTAL 16:9

CHARACTER REFERENCES
{{CHAR_DOCK_WORKERS}}
{{CHAR_ZAHHAK}}

Use the dock-worker references for exactly eight adult workers.
Preserve their individual handmade masks, work clothes, proportions and materials.

Use the Zahhak reference only to preserve the distant observer’s silhouette and staff.
His identity must remain visually unreadable.

LOCATION REFERENCES
{{LOC_COASTAL_RESIDENCE}}
{{LOC_BALCONY}}

PROP REFERENCES
{{PROP_INDUSTRIAL_SAW}}
{{PROP_MOORING_ROPE}}
{{PROP_ZAHHAK_STAFF}}

Preserve the exact referenced saw design.
Do not invent a different blade, additional cutting heads or a conveyor belt.

DIRECTION AND IDENTITY
Create a 20-second live-action cinematic teaser about the physical effort of positioning an enormous timber-cutting machine.

The sequence reveals its weight before revealing its complete shape.

All workers wear their established rigid handmade masks.
Mask geometry and eye openings remain fixed.
Show effort through shoulders, bent knees, grip, breathing and coordinated body weight.

The machine is much larger than an ordinary human-scale woodworking tool.
Its mass must remain consistent across every shot.

Use tactile wood, dark metal, thick rope and worn clothing.
Movement is heavy, slow and physically resisted.

No dialogue.
No narration.
No music.
No titles or readable text.

LOCATION AND LIGHT
Night inside a vast stone collection hall.

The SOUTH entrance is behind the arriving machine.
The machine moves NORTH toward its final position in the center of the hall.
Collection objects stand along the perimeter walls, mostly lost in darkness.

An elevated balcony or gallery occupies the distant NORTH end.

The floor is continuous, flat stone.
The machine’s final position is directly on this floor, not on a raised platform.

One hard, high-mounted neutral work light illuminates the central installation area.

Weak cold night spill enters from the distant balcony opening.

Keep the walls and peripheral displays deeply underexposed.
Use narrow highlights to reveal rope tension, metal edges and the blade’s teeth.

The distant observer remains outside the work-light pool.
Only a faint outline separates him from the dark balcony opening.

No decorative lighting.
No glowing blade.
No sparks.
No smoke or artificial fog.

START STATE AND BLOCKING
Exactly eight masked workers are completing the last short movement of the enormous saw into position.

Four workers pull two thick ropes attached to the lower chassis, two workers per rope.

Two workers push from the rear structural frame.

Two workers guide the sides using heavy handling beams secured to the lower base.

Ropes attach to the structural base, never to the blade.

Use the machine’s established transport wheels or rollers. A low skid edge intermittently scrapes the stone as the frame crosses a shallow floor joint.

The machine remains upright and supported by its transport assembly.

Its blade is completely stationary.
Its motor and cutting mechanism remain OFF throughout.

The unknown observer is already standing motionless beside the distant elevated balcony.

Jamshid does not appear.
No captive, restraint or execution preparation is visible.

SHOT T16-01 | 0s–2s | 2 SECONDS
65mm extreme close-up at floor height beside one enormous wooden-and-metal base member.

A worn skid edge drags across stone under considerable pressure.

Show only this fragment of the structure.
Do not reveal the full machine.

The base advances a few centimeters, catches briefly at a shallow floor joint, then moves again.

Handheld camera tracks alongside this small movement, responding to its uneven friction.

Sound: heavy scraping, timber compression and strained breathing outside the frame.

SHOT T16-02 | 2s–4s | 2 SECONDS
50mm close-up from the side of the forward pulling team.

Several pairs of hands grip the two thick ropes at separate positions.

The ropes run taut out of frame toward the machine behind the workers.

Hands tighten; shoulders and torsos lean into the pull.
One worker resets a foot without releasing tension.

Camera shifts with their shared effort.
Keep the machine itself outside the composition.

SHOT T16-03 | 4s–5s | 1 SECOND
75mm low close-up from beside one heavy transport wheel or roller beneath the base.

It turns slowly under the load.

The wheel, axle and machine remain mechanically connected and consistent with the reference.

Hard cut on a dull wheel impact against the floor joint.

SHOT T16-04 | 5s–6s | 1 SECOND
65mm close-up from a new position beside a metal brace joining the wooden frame.

The loaded connection gives a small physical vibration as the pull continues.

The assembly stays intact.
No breakage or deformation.

SHOT T16-05 | 6s–7s | 1 SECOND
50mm tight oblique on one worker’s hands tightening around the taut rope.

A sleeve draws back slightly under the strain.
The rope stays secured and does not slip free.

Camera is close enough to feel the effort, without obscuring the grip.

SHOT T16-06 | 7s–8s | 1 SECOND
85mm tight detail of a short section of the enormous toothed blade.

As the entire machine advances, a narrow work-light reflection crosses several coarse metal teeth.

The blade does not rotate or reciprocate.
The apparent movement comes only from the whole machine being transported.

Reveal too little of its outline to establish the entire mechanism.

SHOT T16-07 | 8s–13s | 5 SECONDS
24mm handheld medium-wide from the SOUTHWEST side of the hall, looking diagonally NORTH across the machine’s route.

For the first time, reveal most of the enormous timber saw and all eight workers.

The machine occupies the center-right.
The pulling team is ahead of it toward the NORTH, deeper in frame.
The rear pushing pair remains nearer the SOUTH entrance.
The two side guides flank the lower frame.

Move laterally a short distance with the machine, allowing foreground bodies to briefly interrupt the view.

The machine advances slowly toward the central work-light pool.

One side guide loses his footing for half a step.
The adjacent rear worker immediately shifts his shoulder against the secured handling beam, helping maintain direction while the others keep the ropes under tension.

The transport assembly continues supporting the machine’s weight.
No worker catches or lifts the entire machine with his body.

The slipping worker recovers his stance and resumes pushing.

Keep the event brief, awkward and real.
No theatrical fall.
No sudden acceleration.
No machine tipping.

SHOT T16-08 | 13s–17s | 4 SECONDS
28mm low three-quarter wide from the EAST side of the installation position.

This is a new physical camera angle, revealing the full machine across the horizontal frame.

FIRST HALF:
The workers make one final coordinated effort.

The base reaches its floor stop and settles with a single heavy wooden-and-metal impact.

The machine stops completely.

SECOND HALF:
The ropes lose tension and sag.
Workers release their effort and step back from the frame.

Their shoulders remain raised from exertion, then slowly drop.

Hold the complete saw against their smaller bodies.
They look up along its structure in exhausted silence.

The installation feels finished.
The cutting mechanism remains OFF.

SHOT T16-09 | 17s–18s | 1 SECOND
65mm close-up from beside one worker’s shoulder.

He stands next to the now-stationary machine.

His masked head slowly tilts upward toward the distant NORTH balcony.

His visible eyes, if exposed by the reference mask, follow the same direction.

He does not speak or make a theatrical expression.

Cut along his upward eyeline.

SHOT T16-10 | 18s–19s | 1 SECOND
100mm distant long shot from the central hall floor, looking slightly upward toward the NORTH balcony.

A single small silhouette stands beside the dark opening.

Do not cut closer.

The face, costume details, shoulder forms and identity remain unreadable.

The figure is already standing still, supported by a staff.

One small movement settles the staff tip against stone.

Hear one restrained, dry staff contact.
Do not amplify it into a dramatic impact.

SHOT T16-11 | 19s–20s | 1 SECOND
35mm low, locked three-quarter view of the complete saw in the central work-light pool.

The machine is stationary.

The workers remain at its edges, clear of the blade.
The ropes hang slack.

Hold the immense structure, fully positioned and ready.

The blade remains still.
Nothing starts.

CUT TO BLACK at exactly 20 seconds.

END STATE AND EDIT
The machine stands in its final central position on the flat stone floor.

Its full scale has been revealed.
Its intended use has not.

The observer’s identity remains concealed.

No captive arrives.
No cutting occurs.
The machine never powers on.

End immediately after the final stationary image.

SOUND
Only physical, diegetic sound:

stone scraping against the base;
slow loaded wheels or rollers;
wood and metal under strain;
thick rope fibers tightening;
boots searching for traction;
restrained effortful breathing;
one heavy final settling impact;
ropes falling slack;
breathing gradually easing;
one quiet staff contact from the distant balcony.

After the machine settles, allow the room to become quieter naturally.

No spoken orders.
No counting.
No intelligible voices.
No motor startup.
No cutting sound.
No trailer boom or musical sting.

Cut to silence with the final black frame.

Established requirements for this subject:
- No human appears without a mask. Every person on screen, including nobles, gift-bearers, servants and background figures, wears a mask. A figure who is not a named character takes one of the masked caste looks in REF-001, Civilization Caste Board. Never show a bare human face.

<<<image_1>>> is Zahhak (CHR-001 V08); match it wherever Zahhak appears.
<<<image_2>>> is Palace Guards (GRP-005 V01); match it wherever Palace Guards appears.
<<<image_3>>> is Zahhak Hall China (LOC-042 V02); match it wherever Zahhak Hall China appears.
